checks.statement: Aff(1,F_2) has two elements and acts as all permutations of its two points; A_2 is trivial.
checks.reasoning: An affine map has the form x -> ax+b. In F_2 the only nonzero a is 1, and b is 0 or 1, producing the identity and the swap. Only the identity among these two permutations is even.
checks.outcome: The degree-two group comparison and the trivial alternating group are consistent. This does not select the written S subscript between 2 and n.

checks.statement: The degree-three comparison groups have faithful permutation actions of order six; F_3^+ and F_3^* have orders three and two.
checks.reasoning: Aff(1,F_3) has 3 times 2 = 6 distinct affine maps of a three-element set, so its faithful action gives S_3. Gl(2,F_2) has (4-1)(4-2)=6 matrices; its action on the three nonzero vectors is faithful because fixing a basis fixes the linear map. F_2^* has one element, so quotienting Gl(2,F_2) by it changes nothing. Addition in F_3 is cyclic of order three, and F_3^*={1,2} is cyclic of order two.
checks.outcome: The written comparison chain, lower correspondences and quotient are mathematically consistent, without using cardinality alone as a proof of the first two isomorphisms.

checks.statement: A_3 is cyclic of order three.
checks.reasoning: The even permutations on three letters are the identity and the two 3-cycles. A 3-cycle generates these three elements.
checks.outcome: The final A_3 comparison with the additive group of F_3 and Z_3 is consistent; the overwritten letter was read from crop 13 independently.
